root_cause.text: The driver freed DMA buffers used by NTMP commands before ensuring hardware had completed their use, because `netc_xmit_ntmp_cmd()` released the ring lock before the caller finished consuming the response, and also did not abort pending commands on timeout, allowing the hardware to write to already-freed memory.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE description states: "If netc_xmit_ntmp_cmd() times out and returns an error, the pending command is not explicitly aborted, while ntmp_free_data_mem() unconditionally frees the DMA buffer." It also notes: "netc_xmit_ntmp_cmd() releases the ring_lock before the caller finishes consuming the response. At this point, if a concurrent thread submits a new command, it may trigger ntmp_clean_cbdr() and free the DMA buffer while it is still in use." The patch moves ring_lock ownership to the caller and introduces software shadow BDs to track DMA memory, preventing premature freeing.
